verdict.rationale: Pipecat is a framework for real-time voice and multimodal agents, so background automation is a fair axis for it. However, the evidence documents no feature for setting up automations that run on their own, such as scheduled or recurring jobs, background triggers, or unattended workflows. The closest items are developer building blocks: handing off to subagents for long-running tools inside a conversation, multi-agent coordination, and carrier webhooks that start inbound call sessions. None of these is a product-level background automation capability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
